name: uk.co.fileclerk/filing-tools
title: FileClerk
description: UK company filing deadlines, filed figures and iXBRL validation

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Find a UK company's number from its name on the Companies House register: up to 20 matches, each with company_number, company_name, company_status and locality (the town of the registered office), active companies first. Start here when you have a name and no number, then pass company_number to get_company_deadlines, get_company_finances or run_company_tools. name is 2 to 160 characters; a part of the name is enough. Searches have their own limit of 600 per hour.

tools.name: get_company_deadlines
tools.description: Is a UK company in good standing on the Companies House register, and what must happen next? Returns a verdict (act_now, coming_up, all_clear), `nearest` (the nearest open date of all) and one entry per obligation (annual accounts, confirmation statement, each director's and PSC's identity verification, CT600 return and Corporation Tax payment as estimates, payroll when inferred), each with status, due date, basis (register, estimate or inferred), what can happen if missed and its official source. 5 to 8 KB for most companies. `detail: "full"` adds each card's details, risks and official links, the timeline, the track record and register changes, at about 4 times the size. Dates are calendar dates in `timezone`; day counts are for `as_of`. FileClerk is independent, not part of HMRC or Companies House.

tools.name: get_company_finances
tools.description: Filed figures for a UK company from its last 6 annual accounts on the Companies House register, as tagged in the filed iXBRL: net assets, cash, working capital, average employees, the balance sheet lines, and turnover and profit when the company files them (small and micro companies may leave them out, so they are often null). Also who signed the accounts, when, the accounting standard and audit status. A year filed as PDF only takes the prior-year column of the next year's iXBRL accounts (source: comparative); else, once read_scanned_accounts has been called, its scanned pages are read and a figure is kept only when the totals or the OCR digits confirm it (source: pdf-read); scannable is true for a year not read yet, reading while it is queued. FileClerk is independent, not part of HMRC or Companies House.

tools.name: read_scanned_accounts
tools.description: Queue a UK company's accounts filed as scanned PDFs (years where get_company_finances returns scannable: true) to be read by OCR and Claude. Call it only when those years' figures are needed: each read costs FileClerk money and counts against the hourly limit. Reads take minutes; call get_company_finances again later for the figures (years with source pdf-read). A figure is kept only when the totals or the OCR text confirm it.

tools.name: follow_companies
tools.description: Start FileClerk deadline email alerts for up to 50 UK companies at once. FileClerk emails one confirmation link to the address; nothing is sent until the person clicks it. Returns each input as followed, not_found, invalid or duplicate. Use only with the person's own email address and their consent.

tools.name: validate_accounts
tools.description: Check UK company iXBRL accounts (micro-entity, dormant or small, FRS 102 / FRS 105) before filing with Companies House. Pass the whole XHTML file as text (up to 10 MB). Returns one finding per check, the Companies House accounts rules and the company's register record (number, name, status, period end), each reject, risk, not_evaluated or pass with its rule. reject means Companies House rejects it (the V checks are confirmed on its test validator; the R checks find the company missing, closed or under another name); risk means the TIS requires it but rejection is not confirmed. The file is never stored. FileClerk is independent, not part of HMRC or Companies House.

tools.name: prepare_accounts
tools.description: Prepare a dry run for annual accounts. Read registered identity and period defaults, calculate totals and return the checked iXBRL and validation findings. No submission or payment occurs.

tools.name: prepare_ct600
tools.description: Calculate a Company Tax Return (CT600) as a dry run. Pass one set of whole-pound figures for each Corporation Tax accounting period of the accounts. Returns each period's CT600 boxes with HMRC box numbers, the tax and the findings to settle. Nothing is sent to HMRC or stored.

tools.name: get_filing_status
tools.description: Read a FileClerk filing receipt with its signed receipt token. Returns the Companies House status and document paths.

tools.name: request_filing_approval
tools.description: Email a link to the verified owner of a FileClerk API key. The owner uploads the exact checked iXBRL and confirms it before gateway submission can proceed.

tools.name: submit_accounts
tools.description: Check whether the exact accounts have a current human approval. Companies House submission is currently unavailable.

tools.name: find_companies
tools.description: Find UK companies on the Companies House register by filters, without a name: sic (5-digit SIC code), type (ltd, plc, llp, community-interest-company, private-limited-guarant-nsc, limited-partnership, charitable-incorporated-organisation ...), status (active, dissolved, liquidation ...), location (town or postcode), from and to (incorporation dates, YYYY-MM-DD). 50 per page; hits counts every match, pages reach the first 10,000.

tools.name: search_officers
tools.description: Find UK company officers (directors, secretaries, LLP members) by name on the Companies House register: up to 20 matches with officer_id, name and number of appointments. No birth date, nationality or address. Use get_officer with an officer_id for the companies.

tools.name: get_officer
tools.description: Every appointment of one Companies House officer by officer_id (from search_officers): company number and name, role, appointed and resigned dates, company status, current first, with FileClerk's verdict (act_now, coming_up, all_clear) for companies in its cache. Counts as one lookup.

tools.name: list_portfolio
tools.description: Legacy Portfolio link compatibility. Lists followed companies and their next deadlines. For Console, use list_workspace_companies with a workspace key in the Authorization Bearer header, then get_company_deadlines for each company.

tools.name: list_workspace_companies
tools.description: List saved companies, including archived companies, for one Console workspace. Set a workspace API key in the connection's Authorization Bearer header.

tools.name: get_workspace_deadline_settings
tools.description: Read saved Corporation Tax return marks and the key issuer's email categories for one company. Use a workspace key with Manage deadlines permission in the connection's Authorization Bearer header.

tools.name: change_workspace_deadline_settings
tools.description: Change one Corporation Tax return mark or deadline email category. Use a workspace key with Manage deadlines permission in the connection's Authorization Bearer header. For marks send the revision from get_workspace_deadline_settings, or null to create. Send a null kind to clear a mark.

tools.name: set_portfolio_alerts
tools.description: Legacy Portfolio link compatibility. Switch one reminder category for every company on an existing link. For Console, use change_workspace_deadline_settings once per company with a workspace key in the Authorization Bearer header.

tools.name: mark_obligation
tools.description: Legacy Portfolio link compatibility for Corporation Tax return marks. For Console, use get_workspace_deadline_settings to read the mark revision, then change_workspace_deadline_settings with a workspace key in the Authorization Bearer header.

tools.name: calculate_deadlines
tools.description: Work out a UK company's first deadlines from its incorporation date, without a company number: first accounts due date (with the Companies Act 2006 s442 rule used), first confirmation statement, and CT600 and Corporation Tax payment dates (estimates; a first period over 12 months gets two CT periods; none for an LLP). kind is ltd, llp or plc. Give period_end_on only when the first period does not end on the default date (last day of the anniversary month), and shortened_on when an AA01 shortened it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: calculate_penalty
tools.description: Work out UK late filing penalties and interest for given dates: the Companies House accounts penalty (private or public bands, doubled when last year's accounts were also late), CT600 flat penalties by the return's filing date (higher for returns due on or after 1 April 2026; third late in a row is higher), the tax-geared penalty (10% or 20% of unpaid tax) and HMRC late payment interest day by day across rate changes. Money is integer pence. A missing filed or paid date is measured to today. Interest assumes a 365-day year. Nothing is stored.

tools.name: calculate_corporation_tax
tools.description: Work out UK Corporation Tax for a period of accounts (from 1 April 2015, up to 18 months): taxable total profits in whole pounds, the period dates (YYYY-MM-DD) and the number of associated companies. Splits a period over 12 months into two accounting periods and each at 31 March, applies 19%/25% with marginal relief (3/200) from 1 April 2023, reduces the limits for a short period and divides them among associated companies. Returns integer pence per part and per period, with the payment date. Nothing is stored.

tools.name: calculate_s455
tools.description: Work out UK s455 tax on a director's (participator's) loan from a close company for one accounting period (at most 12 months): loans made in the period with dates and whole-pound amounts, repayments with dates, and the balance owed from earlier periods. Each loan at the rate for its date (35.75% from 6 April 2026); repayments clear the oldest debt first; nothing to pay on what is repaid within 9 months and 1 day of the period end; later repayments are reclaims with their earliest date. Warns on the 30-day rule. Integer pence out. Nothing is stored.

tools.name: calculate_income_tax
tools.description: Work out UK take-home pay from gross pay: income tax by band (England, Wales, Northern Ireland, or Scotland's bands from 2017-18), employee Class 1 National Insurance with mid-year rate changes, student loans (plan1, plan2, plan4, plan5, postgraduate) and net pay per year, month and week, for tax years 2011-12 to 2026-27 (tax_year like "2026-27"). gross_pence is pay for one frequency period (year, month, week, day, hour). Standard tax code, no pension. Integer pence out. Nothing is stored.

tools.name: calculate_director_pay
tools.description: Work out a UK company director's salary and dividends for one tax year from 2016-17 (tax_year like "2026-27"): income tax, dividend tax and employee NI for the director; employer NI, Corporation Tax on the profit left and retained profit for the company; and the total tax. profit_pence is the company's profit before the director's salary and employer NI. other_employees: true allows the Employment Allowance. Integer pence in and out. Nothing is stored.

tools.name: check_company_size
tools.description: Is a UK company micro, small, medium or large for its accounts? Uses the limits for financial years beginning on or after 6 April 2025 (two of three: turnover, balance sheet total, average monthly staff), the two-year rule (give last_year, or first_year: true; and last_size when one year meets a limit and the other misses it), and pro-rates turnover by months. Returns the size, what it may file, and whether it is exempt from audit, each with its Companies Act section. Money in whole pounds. Nothing is stored.

tools.name: check_strike_off
tools.description: Can a UK company apply to be struck off the register (DS01) now? Reads the Companies House register (status, filings in the last 3 months, a strike-off already applied for, outstanding charges) and takes three answers: traded or sold stock, an open insolvency or court case, other activity, each in the last 3 months (true means yes; leave out to get verdict answer_questions). Returns can_apply, not_yet with each bar and its Companies Act section, or closed, plus warnings and the steps (fee, 7-day copy duty). Counts as one lookup.

tools.name: check_2028_filing
tools.description: From 1 April 2028 UK company accounts must be filed by software as iXBRL. For 1 to 50 company numbers, returns how each company's latest annual accounts were filed (paper, pdf, webfiling or software) and must_move or ready, with no_accounts, not_found, invalid, unknown or limit otherwise. Each number counts as one lookup on the hourly limit.

tools.name: run_company_tools
tools.description: Every FileClerk tool on one UK company at once: how its last accounts were filed and whether it must move to software by 1 April 2028; whether it can apply to be struck off (pass traded, insolvency and activity as true or false; leave out for verdict answer_questions); its size from the two newest filed accounts (null when they carry too few figures); and the accounts late filing penalty if filed today (null without a due date). Counts as one lookup.
